subject: Biology
source: Paraphrased exemplars in the style of Edexcel GCSE (9-1) Biology 1BI0 Papers 1 and 2 (2018 onwards). Stems are author-original; mark allocations follow Edexcel mark scheme conventions.

exemplars.stem: State the function of the mitochondria in an animal cell, and the function of the cell membrane.
exemplars.markScheme: 1 mark: mitochondria — site of (aerobic) respiration / where energy is released. 1 mark: cell membrane — controls movement of substances in and out of the cell.
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1BI0 Paper 1F style — cell organelle function

exemplars.stem: A student investigated the effect of pH on the activity of amylase. Outline a method the student could use to find the pH at which amylase works fastest, including how they would measure rate, and identify two control variables.
exemplars.markScheme: Method (4 marks): mix amylase with starch at chosen pH (using buffers); take samples at intervals; test with iodine for absence of starch; record time taken for iodine to stop turning blue-black. Control variables (2 marks): two of — temperature; concentration of amylase; concentration of starch; volume of buffer.
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1BI0 Core Practical style — enzyme pH investigation

exemplars.stem: A 5 cm cube of potato has a mass of 5.0 g before being placed in distilled water. After 1 hour the cube has a mass of 5.4 g. Calculate the percentage change in mass and explain why the mass changed.
exemplars.markScheme: M1 for percentage change calc (0.4/5.0 × 100). A1 for +8%. 1 mark: water moved into the cells by osmosis (down water potential gradient).
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1BI0 Paper 1 style — osmosis percentage change

exemplars.stem: Describe how an impulse passes from one neurone to another at a synapse.
exemplars.markScheme: 1 mark: impulse arrives at end of pre-synaptic neurone. 1 mark: triggers release of neurotransmitter into the synaptic gap. 1 mark: neurotransmitter diffuses across the gap. 1 mark: binds to receptors on post-synaptic neurone, triggering a new impulse.
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1BI0 Paper 1H style — synaptic transmission (HT mechanism)

exemplars.stem: A father is heterozygous for the cystic fibrosis allele (Ff) and a mother is heterozygous (Ff). Cystic fibrosis is caused by a recessive allele (f). Use a Punnett square to determine the probability that any one child will have cystic fibrosis.
exemplars.markScheme: M1 for Punnett square with parental gametes F, f and F, f. M1 for offspring FF, Ff, Ff, ff. M1 for identifying ff as cystic fibrosis. A1 for 1/4 (or 25%).

exemplars.stem: Explain how natural selection can lead to a population of bacteria becoming resistant to an antibiotic over many generations.
exemplars.markScheme: 1 mark: variation in the bacterial population caused by random mutation. 1 mark: some bacteria, by chance, are resistant to the antibiotic. 1 mark: when antibiotic is used, non-resistant bacteria are killed; resistant ones survive. 1 mark: resistant bacteria reproduce, passing on resistance allele, so population becomes more resistant.
exemplars.source: Edexcel 1BI0 Paper 2 style — natural selection in bacteria

exemplars.stem: Describe how a vaccination protects a person against a particular bacterial disease.
exemplars.markScheme: 1 mark: vaccine contains weakened/dead pathogen or antigen. 1 mark: stimulates white blood cells to produce specific antibodies. 1 mark: memory cells remain so that on second exposure antibodies are produced quickly and the person doesn't become ill.
